title: Colour
slide_intent: Teach designers to select the mark’s foreground in relation to its background so the seal remains visible.
strategic_value: Sheffield Museums can use its palette across varied materials while keeping the trust mark identifiable.
demonstration: Two equal square fields compare a white seal on dark blue with a black seal on pink, each labeled by foreground and background treatment.
practical_value: Choose the light or dark mark after inspecting the value of the intended background.

content_islands.name: Contrast guidance
content_islands.spec: Use the left column to explain the palette and the need to preserve clarity.

content_islands.name: Paired foreground examples
content_islands.spec: Align two equal fields with the same mark at the same scale. Use white on dark blue and black on pink. Caption both below.

reference_purposes.Expression: The paired specimens show a white museum seal on dark blue and a black seal on pink.
reference_purposes.Application: The captioned examples pair the seal foreground with light and dark backgrounds.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The text requires the chosen combination to keep the logo clear and accessible.

ingredient.name: Museum seal color
ingredient.role: Keep the shared museum identifier readable across different backgrounds.
ingredient.application: The guide permits any brand-palette color for the seal and often uses black or white. Check that the chosen combination remains clear and accessible.
ingredient.scope: Sheffield Museums parent seal. The two specimens demonstrate common choices rather than restricting the logo to those two combinations.
